feature: A sound's trim grip trims wherever you grab it
summary: Pressing anywhere on the white trim grip at either end of a picked sound now trims it. Before, a press in the grip's middle caught the volume line running across it and nudged the volume instead.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open the Sample Talk recording (File > Open Sample) with the timeline open.

try.do: Click the middle of the sound under V1 to pick it.
Press the white grip at the sound's start in its middle, where the volume line crosses it, and drag right.
Press ⌘Z, then drag the volume line down from the middle of the segment.
Press the start grip in its middle again and drag right.
Press ⌘Z, drag the volume line all the way up, then drag the end grip left from its middle.

evaluate: Does every press on a grip trim, wherever on the grip you press?
Can you still grab the volume line easily everywhere between the two grips?
Does the volume line passing under the white grip, rather than over it, look right to you?
rough: No mock covers this: video-audio.html draws no trim grip on a sound segment, so there is no frame to set this beside.

Within about five points either side of a grip the grip now wins over the volume line, so the line cannot be grabbed right at the clip's very edge; the fade diamond and the rest of the line are unchanged.
